correctness.rationale: The proof checks exact defining quadratic forms for the apex and both cube vertex orbits in all three parameter intervals, reconstructs a valid centered isotropic contact measure with full covariance I_d/d, and uses a trace–determinant AM–GM inequality to rule out every smaller translated or oriented ellipsoid. Boundary values and all equality contacts are checked. Rational checker verify.py was executed and returned 50,022 exact configurations plus 4,200 sampled vertex diagnostics. The high-dimensional limit is obtained by an explicit log expansion, not numerical extrapolation. Finite diagnostics do not stand in for the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The minimum covering ellipsoid of a cube enlarged by a single axial point is an intrinsically motivated robustness and design geometry problem. The complete d-dimensional answer has two analytically sharp and different geometric transitions, exact unique center and semiaxes, full contact classification and optimal contact weights, and an exponential high-dimensional limit. This is a complete nontrivial natural family, not a routine algebraic substitution, isolated data point or arbitrary slice.
